newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Iraqi 'oil-for-food' proceeds near $200 million.
newsitem.headline: Iraqi 'oil-for-food' proceeds near $200 million.

text.p: An escrow account holding the proceeds from the sale of Iraqi oil is expected to reach a total of nearly $200 million by Monday, a U.N. spokesman said on Friday.

The account at the New York branch of the Banque Nationale de Paris was opened under an oil-for-food deal that became effective on Dec. 10. The deal enables Iraq to sell $2 billion of oil over six months to buy food, medicine and other humanitarian supplies to help offset the effects of sanctions imposed since its 1990 invasion of Kuwait.

The U.N. spokesman said $23 million was due to be paid into the escrow account later on Friday and a further $23.6 million on Monday. These sums are in addition to $68.8 million on Jan. 15, $44 million on Jan. 16 and $35.7 million on Jan. 21.
The spokesman gave no details of the oil contracts that produced those sums.

So far, $53.1 million has been disbursed from the account, including $33.9 million for the Geneva-based U.N. compensation commission that rules on reparations for victims of the Iraqi invasion. The remainder went for various other U.N. activities related to the war.
Thirty percent of the proceeds of the Iraqi oil sales are earmarked for reparations.

The Security Council's Iraqi sanctions committee, which monitors exports to Iraq, approved on Thursday a $50 million sale of Australian wheat and about $21 million of rice from Thailand. The committee is still considering the proposed sale to Iraq of detergent powder from Vietnam, which a U.N. source said was worth about $5 million.

Under U.N. procedures, it approves contracts for the sale of food and medicine on a 48-hour no-objection basis -- meaning a deal is automatically approved if no member of the 15-nation committee raises objections during that period.
Non-food items are approved if no objections are raised during a seven-day grace period.
